product_frame.who: Linux desktop users running Caelune as a Wayland shell, including people installing it for the first time, repeatedly launching apps, and playing games on both weak and powerful hardware.
product_frame.job: Find, install, launch, switch, and manage desktop applications while keeping system feedback and recovery visible.
product_frame.consequence: A failed install, lost window, hidden notification, or GPU failure can strand the user or cause data loss, so the shell must explain state and preserve a fallback path.
product_frame.primary_action: Select one application and either launch it or start an explicit Flatpak install.
product_frame.frequency: Catalog discovery is occasional; app launching and window switching are repeated throughout a session.
product_frame.risk_level: medium-high for install, swap, and window lifecycle actions; low for browsing
product_frame.device_profile: Keyboard/pointer desktop first, with narrow nested-host layouts and touch-sized hit areas where space permits; official Linux targets are Mint, Ubuntu, and Arch.
secondary_actions: Change notification, graphics, and Game Mode preferences
Inspect workload evidence and restore the previous profile
product_frame.surface_type: native app-shell / catalog / settings / compositor workspace

experience_archetype.evidence: A catalog requires orientation and curiosity, while a desktop shell requires stable placement, low-latency keyboard continuity, and recoverable state.
experience_archetype.impact_if_false: If OPERATE dominates every surface, the gallery becomes a dense utility list; if EXPLORE dominates settings and windows, repeated actions become slow and disorienting.

product_frame.frequency_density: Gallery discovery is occasional; launching and switching windows is frequent and must stay compact. The shell should support 3/30/300 installed entries through filtering and bounded rendering rather than unbounded tiles.
product_frame.device_input: Wide desktop pointer/keyboard first, with narrow host-window and touch-like pointer coordinates treated as supported adaptations; Super shortcuts, Tab cycling, Escape, Enter, and focus-visible states are required.
product_frame.content_truth: Installed applications come from freedesktop desktop entries and Flatpak metadata; system notices come from real command results; absent tools and offline remotes are shown as unavailable rather than simulated.
product_frame.success_state: The chosen app is mapped/running, an install has a confirmed result, a notification is either read or intentionally disabled, or a window is visibly focused/arranged.

Initial backend, startup, notification, and optional swap choices are persisted with recovery.

constraints.platform: Linux Wayland compositor in Rust 2024; official support targets Mint, Ubuntu, and Arch. Winit nested backend exists today while native session work is added.
constraints.graphics: Vulkan preferred when available; OpenGL is the required fallback and software/opaque rendering is the last resort; Liquid Glass effects remain bounded and optional on low-end hardware.
constraints.external: Flatpak/Flathub, nmcli, pactl, system files, and package managers can be missing or offline.
constraints.safety: Swapfile and installer actions must be explicit, idempotent, permission-aware, and dry-runnable.
constraints.performance: Avoid full-output blur, unbounded animation, per-frame allocations, and background work while hidden; use low-end budgets and real measurements before speed claims.

existing_system.stack_ref: Rust compatibility crate rouch 0.1.0 (public product name Caelune); Smithay 0.7; Winit nested backend with renderer_gl; pure models for launcher, Finder, settings, widgets, dock, chrome, windowing, and workload detection.
existing_patterns: pure geometry/state modules with renderer sampling
real system reads/writes in linux backends
GlassRecipe with reduced-transparency and battery policies
shared shell shortcut resolution and finite pointer hit-testing with primary-button ownership
missing_or_risky: native DRM/libinput and XWayland remain outside current nested milestone
PTY and VT runtime on Linux needs hardware/session verification
installer system mutation and setup persistence
game detector and resource policy need Linux process/window/cgroup verification; false positives must remain reversible

invariants: No external command result is presented as success until its exit status and output say so.
Every GPU path has a working OpenGL or opaque fallback and a diagnosable failure state.
A notification setting change is reflected in both persisted preference and live routing before the control settles.
The active window is reachable, visible, and represented in MRU order after focus, minimize, maximize, fullscreen, close, and workspace changes.
Install, swap, and startup configuration operations are idempotent and never silently overwrite user data.
Keyboard focus order and visible focus survive gallery, settings, notification, window-switcher, and error states.
Game Mode only changes bounded, explicitly named shell policies after confidence/evidence checks; it snapshots those policies and restores them when the game session ends.

information_architecture.nav_model: Persistent shell anchors: top bar for system status/notifications, dock for pinned/running apps, window space for work, and anchored sheets for gallery/settings/notifications.
information_architecture.sequence: entry -> orient with search/status -> inspect app/window -> act install/launch/focus -> receive settlement -> continue or recover
information_architecture.disclosure: Show action state and source first; reveal version, command diagnostics, cache age, swap plan, and GPU details on demand.
information_architecture.responsive_transforms: At intermediate/narrow widths, app detail moves below results, sidebars become a selectable sheet, notification stack becomes a full-width tray, and window switcher keeps one focused row/preview at a time.
failure_recovery: launch installed app without Flatpak remote

accessibility_contract.semantics: Use native keyboard/focus semantics in the compositor model and expose accessible names for every app, notification, control, and window action.
accessibility_contract.focus: Gallery search is first focus on open; Settings exposes a sidebar/content focus ring and skips status-only rows; sheets trap/restore focus where appropriate; Escape closes transient surfaces; Alt-Tab release restores focus to selected window; pointer focus and keyboard focus expose the same action target.
accessibility_contract.contrast: Text and icons use opaque backing in worst wallpaper frames; selected/error/disabled states are not color-only.
accessibility_contract.motion: Reduced-motion and reduced-transparency preferences are authored variants; no essential meaning depends on blur, bounce, or continuous movement.
accessibility_contract.targets: Pointer targets are at least 24x24 CSS-equivalent logical pixels, with ~44px ergonomic targets for primary desktop controls when space allows; hover is supplementary and never the only indication of an action.
accessibility_contract.async: Install, backend probing, and notification insertion announce state changes without stealing focus; failures name cause and next action.
accessibility_contract.reflow: Long localized labels wrap or disclose without clipping at narrow widths and text scale.

perf_budget.image_strategy: Decode wallpaper once, reserve icon bounds, lazy-load non-visible catalog art, and use opaque color fallback when image/GPU paths fail.
perf_budget.font_budget: Use installed system font or one fallback; no remote font fetch.
interaction_latency_concerns: search/filter should avoid scanning on every draw
pointer motion should coalesce and redraw only when hit/hover state changes
Alt-Tab must not allocate unbounded previews
Flatpak subprocess output must not block the event loop
PTY output must be drained without blocking the compositor and scrollback must stay bounded
Game Mode detection should sample on a timer/event boundary, not scan processes every frame

evidence_refs.claim: Current shell already models top bar, dock, launcher, settings, Game Mode presentation rows, widgets, wallpaper, chrome, and nested OpenGL rendering.
Nested input forwards pointer motion to clients while suppressing redundant shell redraws, reserves shell shortcuts before client forwarding, and gates shell activation to the primary pointer button.
Flatpak and Vulkan are host capabilities and may be missing; degraded behavior is a product requirement, not a test shortcut.
Native DRM/libinput, real Flathub network access, Vulkan context-loss recovery, and rendered wide/mid/narrow screenshots require a Linux runtime matrix.
